note: PROPOSED by the Lead Architect on 2026-09-29 as the V1 roadmap of wOS itself (dogfood). It has NOT been through Astra/Fable review; weights and requirements are the architect's first reasoning, not consensus. The V1 build is tracked against it exactly like a target (docs/architecture/WORKSTREAMS.md). Updated for D13 (2026-09-29): surfaces, journeys, per-surface weights and the multi-surface capability.

items.title: Email magic-link sign-in
items.description: Anyone signs in with a single-use email link or code; accounts are created by verified email (D8).

items.title: GitHub identity link
items.description: A contributor links one GitHub account, required before any lease, review, proposal or resolution (D8).

items.title: Desktop and CLI sessions
items.description: Short-lived wOS sessions held in the OS keychain on Desktop and CLI; no model credentials ever handled (D1, D5).

items.title: Contributor profile and settings
items.description: A contributor sees their history, settings and leaderboard opt-in.

items.title: Sniper Targets
items.description: Real targets exist in the control plane with their public status.

items.title: Global Feature Catalog
items.description: One app-independent catalog of features referenced by many roadmaps (D10).

items.title: Canonical Application Roadmap PR
items.description: One canonical active roadmap PR per application; contributors propose into it.

items.title: Roadmap Astra and Fable review rounds
items.description: Both reviewers independently try to prove the roadmap incomplete until NO MATERIAL GAPS, then ROADMAP CONSENSUS.

items.title: Reasoned feature weights
items.description: Every capability and feature carries a reasoned weight frozen with the roadmap version (D12).

items.title: Feature Contract consensus
items.description: Feature Contracts reach consensus through the same independent review loop.

items.title: Build Graph of Atomic Build Units
items.description: A merged Feature Contract yields a dependency-aware Build Graph of ABUs sized for one Opus agent.

items.title: Proposals (wos propose)
items.description: Contributors propose roadmap or contract changes through wOS.

items.title: Architecture conflict resolution (wos resolve)
items.description: Escalated disputes and blockers are ruled on by the Architecture Conflict Resolver.

items.title: Agent and model eligibility
items.description: wOS checks agent/model eligibility before issuing work (step 8).

items.title: Leases and logical locks
items.description: Leases with heartbeats; ABUs from one feature leased simultaneously without overlapping write or logical ownership.

items.title: Isolated worktrees on immutable base commits
items.description: Each lease builds in its own git worktree pinned to an immutable base commit.

items.title: Deterministic role-specific context
items.description: Every invocation gets its own context and an immutable Context Manifest; context budgets reject oversize ABUs.

items.title: Machine-readable Agent Policies
items.description: Reviewer and builder requirements live in Agent Policy data, including max reasoning per provider.

items.title: Local Claude Code and Codex launch
items.description: wOS launches the contributor's own claude and codex CLIs with the policy's model and reasoning (D1).

items.title: Scope enforcement and diff validation
items.description: Allowed and forbidden paths enforced; symlinks, workflows, lockfiles and generated files rejected.

items.title: Deterministic verification
items.description: Typecheck, lint, tests and acceptance checks locally and again in CI (D2).

items.title: Independent implementation reviews
items.description: Astra and Fable review each contribution on other contributors' machines at maximum reasoning (D2).

items.title: Qualification
items.description: Machine-checked qualification before any official PR (D9).

items.title: Gated PRs by the GitHub App
items.description: Only the wOS GitHub App opens PRs, after qualification; contributors never push (D9).

items.title: Contribution provenance
items.description: Every PR records who built and reviewed it, with which model, context and checks.

items.title: Merge handling and unlocking
items.description: Merge updates build progress and unlocks dependent ABUs.

items.title: wOS Desktop
items.description: Electron app: sign in, browse the Sniper List, drill down, press BUILD, watch agents, history, settings.

items.title: Desktop security boundary
items.description: Renderer without Node; secure IPC and context isolation; signed and notarised in CI (D7).

items.title: wOS CLI
items.description: wos build, roadmap, propose, resolve, review and status on the same orchestration as Desktop.

items.title: Sniper List with real progress
items.description: Homepage lists targets with MAPPED, SPECIFIED and BUILT, 0% when nothing exists.

items.title: Drilldown pages
items.description: Application -> capability -> feature -> requirement -> ABU -> contribution/PR pages.

items.title: Latest activity
items.description: Public activity feed from real events.

items.title: Contributor profiles and opt-in leaderboard
items.description: Public profiles, reward history and an opt-in leaderboard.

items.title: Hosted and self-hosted status
items.description: Each application shows whether it is hosted and whether it can be self-hosted.

items.title: Append-only WOS token ledger
items.description: One unit, append-only, balances derived, debits supported (D3).

items.title: Reward rules for accepted work
items.description: Rewards for accepted roadmap, contract, resolution, implementation, review and security work; none for opening a PR.

items.title: Completion pools
items.description: Feature and application completion pools.

items.title: Migration ledger and ship gate
items.description: Schema migrations applied only by a ship gate with a ledger (D7).

items.title: Integration waves and end-to-end tests
items.description: Integration tests across workstreams, simultaneous builders, leases and concurrency.

items.title: Security hardening
items.description: Adversarial tests of the gate, the ledger, reviews and scope.

items.title: Transactional email
items.description: Sign-in and notification mail from a sending subdomain (D5, D8).

items.title: Multi-repo products
items.description: Build graphs whose ABUs live in several repositories of one family, each ABU in exactly one repo (D13).

items.title: Toolchain eligibility
items.description: An ABU touching native code is leasable only on a device whose attested toolchain (macOS + Xcode, Android SDK) meets the repo's path-based requirements (D13).

items.title: Native CI runners
items.description: Native iOS builds and end-to-end checks on macOS runners, everything else on Linux, keeping Apple-machine minutes low (D13).

items.title: Per-surface acceptance
items.description: Journey acceptance per surface: Playwright across the browser matrix for web, Maestro flows for iOS and Android (D13).

items.title: Mobile app signing and delivery
items.description: EAS Build signs and delivers the replacement apps' iOS and Android builds in CI only, with credentials separate from wOS Desktop's (D7, D13).

roadmap.summary: wOS V1: the platform that lets contributors build open-source replacements with their own AI agents, from roadmap consensus to gated, reviewed, rewarded pull requests, with a public website of honest progress.

architecture.overview: Monorepo waronsaas/wos: control plane (Hono on Vercel, Postgres on Supabase), Electron Desktop and a CLI over one shared orchestrator package, and the Next.js public site. See docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md.
architecture.composition: Shared packages (contracts, db, agent-policy, context-engine, verification, github, planning, rewards, orchestrator) composed by services/control-plane, apps/desktop, apps/cli and apps/web.
architecture.appSpecificData: Everything lives in the wos Postgres schema defined by packages/db/migrations.
architecture.selfHosting: Not a V1 goal for wOS itself; the control plane is one Vercel project plus one Supabase database.

catalog.title: Activity and profiles
catalog.summary: Public activity feed, contributor profiles, reward history and opt-in leaderboard.

catalog.title: Agent policy
catalog.summary: Machine-readable rules for which agent, model and reasoning level may perform each role.

catalog.title: Build graph validation
catalog.summary: Deterministic validation that a build graph of atomic units is acyclic, covered, parallel-safe and within budget.

catalog.title: Context engine
catalog.summary: Deterministic, role-specific agent context with immutable manifests and budgets.

catalog.title: Contributor profile
catalog.summary: A person's public profile, contribution history and settings.

catalog.title: Device sessions
catalog.summary: Short-lived access and rotating refresh sessions per device, stored in the OS keychain.

catalog.title: Feature catalog
catalog.summary: A global, app-independent catalog of features that many application roadmaps reference.

catalog.title: Feature contract consensus
catalog.summary: A canonical, versioned feature contract with per-app requirement profiles reviewed to consensus.

catalog.title: Gated pull requests
catalog.summary: Pull requests opened only by an app, only after machine-checked qualification.

catalog.title: GitHub identity link
catalog.summary: Link, unlink and reserve one GitHub identity per account for contribution and provenance.

catalog.title: Integration and end-to-end tests
catalog.summary: Cross-workstream integration waves and end-to-end tests including simultaneous builders.

catalog.title: Leases and locks
catalog.summary: Time-bounded exclusive work leases with path and logical resource locks.

catalog.title: Local orchestrator
catalog.summary: The shared local driver of lease, build, verify, review, qualify and PR steps.

catalog.title: Email magic-link sign-in
catalog.summary: Passwordless sign-in by a single-use emailed link or code, bound to the client that started it.

catalog.title: Mobile app signing
catalog.summary: CI-only signing and delivery of iOS and Android builds with credentials separate from other apps.

catalog.title: Multi-repo products
catalog.summary: Build graphs whose units live in several repositories of one family, each unit in exactly one repository.

catalog.title: Native CI runners
catalog.summary: Linux runners for everything except native builds and end-to-end checks, which run on macOS runners.

catalog.title: Per-surface acceptance
catalog.summary: Journey acceptance checks per surface: browser-matrix web tests and mobile flow tests.

catalog.title: Progress drilldown
catalog.summary: Public pages from application to capability, feature, requirement, unit and PR, with traceable numbers.

catalog.title: Proposals and resolution
catalog.summary: Proposals into canonical documents and rulings on escalated disputes and blockers.

catalog.title: Provenance and merge
catalog.summary: Provenance records for every accepted change and merge handling that unlocks dependents.

catalog.title: Review rounds
catalog.summary: Sealed, independent two-reviewer rounds with a finding ledger and atomic reveal.

catalog.title: Reward rules
catalog.summary: Rules that turn accepted contributions into ledger entries, holds, reversals and pools.

catalog.title: Roadmap consensus
catalog.summary: A canonical, versioned roadmap per application reviewed independently until no material gaps remain.

catalog.title: Scope verification
catalog.summary: Deterministic validation of a submission against allowed and forbidden paths and resources.

catalog.title: Security hardening
catalog.summary: Adversarial testing of gates, ledgers, reviews and scope enforcement.

catalog.title: Ship gate and migrations
catalog.summary: A migration runner with a ledger, applied only by a gate that refuses unsafe deploys.

catalog.title: Sniper List site
catalog.summary: The public list of targets with honest progress.

catalog.title: Token ledger
catalog.summary: An append-only, hash-chained ledger of in-app credits with derived balances.

catalog.title: Toolchain eligibility
catalog.summary: Path-based toolchain requirements per repository matched against attested contributor toolchains at claim time.

catalog.title: Transactional email
catalog.summary: Sign-in and notification email from a sending subdomain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC.

catalog.summary: The command-line contributor client.

requirements.statement: Activity MUST show only public events and profiles MUST show scores only for opted-in contributors.
acceptance: A contributor who did not opt in has no score on their profile.

requirements.statement: Each role MUST specify allowed models, required reasoning, sandbox, tools, budget, lease timing, independence and obligations as data.
acceptance: The policy document parses against its schema.

requirements.statement: Eligibility MUST refuse a reviewer who authored the subject or holds the other slot of the round, except under labelled bootstrap rules.
acceptance: An author claiming a review of their own attempt is refused.

requirements.statement: The validator MUST reject cycles, uncovered requirements, parallel ABUs with overlapping write scopes or exclusive resources, and ABUs over the builder context budget.
acceptance: Each rejection is reported with its error code and ABU key.

requirements.statement: The same context plan and snapshot MUST produce a byte-identical prompt and manifest.
acceptance: Two runs over the same inputs produce the same manifest sha256.

requirements.statement: A reviewer's context MUST NOT include the other slot's verdict for the current round.
acceptance: Manifests of both reviewers of a round contain no reference to the other's verdict.

requirements.statement: A contributor MUST be able to see their contributions, token history and leaderboard opt-in, and change the opt-in.
acceptance: Toggling opt-in adds or removes the contributor from the public leaderboard.

requirements.statement: Refresh tokens MUST rotate on use and reuse of a rotated token MUST revoke the whole session family.
acceptance: Replaying an old refresh token revokes every session in the family.

requirements.statement: Desktop and CLI MUST store the session only in the OS keychain.
acceptance: No session material is written to plain files.

requirements.statement: Every roadmap feature reference MUST resolve to exactly one active catalog feature.
acceptance: A roadmap referencing an unknown or aliased feature fails validation.

requirements.statement: A duplicate catalog feature MUST be mergeable into another by an alias change that carries its requirements and profiles.
acceptance: After an alias merge, apps that referenced the duplicate show the target feature.

requirements.statement: A feature contract MUST contain one requirement profile per app that references the feature and has been specified.
acceptance: Salesforce and HubSpot profiles can list different requirement ids of one contract.

requirements.statement: A new version of a shared contract MUST list every impacted app, and reviewers MUST receive those apps' profiles.
acceptance: A version without impactedTargets fails validation.

requirements.statement: Only the wOS GitHub App MUST open official PRs, and only after qualification succeeded.
acceptance: A PR opened by any other author is closed automatically.

requirements.statement: The App MUST build commits from validated submissions via the Git Data API with a Co-authored-by trailer for the contributor.
acceptance: The PR commit's tree equals the reviewed candidate tree.

requirements.statement: An account MUST link at most one GitHub identity, and a GitHub identity MUST be linked to at most one account.
acceptance: Linking a GitHub already linked elsewhere returns GITHUB_LINKED_ELSEWHERE.

requirements.statement: Unlinking MUST be refused while the account holds an active lease, live attempt or sealed review, and the unlinked identity MUST stay reserved to the account for 90 days.
acceptance: Unlink during an active lease returns 409.
Linking a reserved identity to another account returns GITHUB_RESERVED.

requirements.statement: The end-to-end suite MUST run two builders on independent ABUs of one feature at the same time without conflicts.
acceptance: Both attempts reach pr_open and merge cleanly.

requirements.statement: A task MUST have at most one active lease, and leases MUST expire when heartbeats stop.
acceptance: A lease without heartbeats expires after its TTL and the task reopens.

requirements.statement: Two ABUs MUST NOT be in progress at once when their write scopes overlap or they claim the same exclusive resource.
acceptance: Claiming an ABU whose scope overlaps a live attempt returns RESOURCE_LOCKED.

requirements.statement: Desktop and CLI MUST drive every workflow through the same orchestrator interface.
acceptance: The CLI and Desktop produce identical event streams for the same fake run.

requirements.statement: The orchestrator MUST launch claude and codex with the model, reasoning and restrictions the Agent Policy requires.
acceptance: describeInvocation output matches the policy for every role.

requirements.statement: A sign-in token MUST be single-use, expire within 15 minutes and be stored only as a sha256 hash.
acceptance: Redeeming the same link twice fails the second time.
A token older than 15 minutes is rejected.

requirements.statement: Redemption MUST require the poll secret held by the client that started the sign-in.
acceptance: A link opened by a different client cannot complete another client's sign-in.

requirements.statement: The start endpoint MUST return the same response whether or not the email has an account, and MUST rate-limit per email and per IP.
acceptance: Responses for known and unknown emails are byte-identical apart from ids.
The sixth start for one email within an hour is refused.

requirements.statement: Mobile signing credentials MUST exist only in the CI release environment and MUST be separate from wOS Desktop's signing identity.
acceptance: No workflow outside the release environment can read the signing secrets.

requirements.statement: Every ABU MUST name exactly one repository, and a build graph MAY span repositories of the same family with dependencies by global ABU key.
acceptance: An ABU in a repository outside its contract's family is rejected by the database.

requirements.statement: Only checks that need native builds MUST run on macOS runners; typecheck, lint and unit tests MUST run on Linux.
acceptance: The workflow's macOS jobs are limited to native build and end-to-end steps.

requirements.statement: Each profile MUST have one acceptance check per surface named wos-acceptance/<feature>/<target>/<surface>, and web acceptance MUST run the full browser matrix.
acceptance: A web acceptance run missing Firefox fails validation.

requirements.statement: A feature MUST NOT count as BUILT on a surface until that surface's acceptance check passed on the default branch.
acceptance: An iOS pass does not complete Android.

requirements.statement: Every percentage MUST link to the weights and records it was computed from.
acceptance: From any app percentage a visitor can reach the PRs behind it.

requirements.statement: wos propose MUST record a proposal that the next author round sees and answers.
acceptance: An accepted proposal appears in the next revision's proposals list.

requirements.statement: An escalated finding MUST be ruled upheld or overruled by a resolver and confirmed by a maintainer before the workflow continues.
acceptance: An unconfirmed ruling keeps the document escalated.

requirements.statement: Every official PR MUST have a provenance record naming builders, reviewers, models, reasoning, manifests and CI results.
acceptance: The provenance record hash is shown in the PR body.

requirements.statement: A merge MUST mark the ABU merged, unlock dependents and trigger progress recomputation.
acceptance: A dependent ABU becomes ready after its last dependency merges.

requirements.statement: Verdicts MUST stay sealed until both slots have submitted, then be revealed atomically.
acceptance: A reviewer cannot read the other slot's verdict before reveal.

requirements.statement: Verdicts MUST be bound to the reviewed head sha and submission hash.
acceptance: A verdict for a different head sha is rejected.

requirements.statement: Accepted work MUST earn tokens exactly once per unit, never for merely opening a PR.
acceptance: Replaying the same acceptance event writes no second award.

requirements.statement: A per-app completion pool MUST fire when that app's profile of a feature is complete.
acceptance: Completing HubSpot's profile of a shared feature does not fire Salesforce's pool.

requirements.statement: There MUST be at most one open roadmap workflow per application.
acceptance: Opening a second roadmap for the same app returns 409.

requirements.statement: A roadmap MUST reach consensus only when both reviewer slots return NO_MATERIAL_GAPS on the same head sha in the same round.
acceptance: One MATERIAL_GAPS verdict sends the roadmap back to revision.

requirements.statement: Every capability and feature MUST carry a weight with a written rationale, and weights MUST sum to 10000 at each level.
acceptance: A roadmap missing a rationale or with wrong sums fails schema validation.

requirements.statement: Submissions touching protected, generated, workflow or symlink paths, or lockfiles and migrations without the declared resource, MUST be rejected.
acceptance: Each forbidden case is rejected with its error code.

requirements.statement: The test suite MUST attempt modified-client submissions, fabricated verdicts, self-review and path escapes, and each MUST be refused.
acceptance: Every adversarial case in SECURITY.md has a test that fails if the defence is removed.

requirements.statement: Production MUST be migrated only by the ship gate, which refuses a dirty tree, an unpushed commit or red CI.
acceptance: Running the gate with a dirty tree exits non-zero before migrating.

requirements.statement: The site MUST show MAPPED, SPECIFIED and BUILT for every target from live data, and 0% when nothing exists.
acceptance: No target shows a number that the API does not return.

requirements.statement: Ledger entries MUST be append-only and hash-chained, and balances MUST be derived, never stored.
acceptance: UPDATE and DELETE on the ledger fail for every role.

requirements.statement: A claim of an ABU whose write scope touches a repo's toolchain-requirement paths MUST be refused unless the device's latest toolchain attestation satisfies that requirement.
acceptance: A Linux device cannot claim an ABU writing apps/mobile/ios/**.
The same device can claim a JS-only mobile ABU.

requirements.statement: Mail MUST be sent from a subdomain with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, leaving the apex MX untouched.
acceptance: Sign-in mail passes DMARC alignment in a Gmail inbox.

requirements.statement: The CLI MUST provide wos build, roadmap, propose, resolve, review and status over the shared orchestrator.
acceptance: Each command appears in wos --help and calls the orchestrator.

requirements.statement: The renderer MUST run sandboxed with context isolation and no Node access; privileged work MUST happen in the main process.
acceptance: window.require and process are undefined in the renderer.

requirements.statement: A contributor MUST be able to sign in, pick Salesforce -> CRM -> a feature -> an eligible ABU, and press BUILD.
acceptance: The BUILD button starts the shared orchestrator and streams its events.
